commit_reviews.summary: The feature maps to the story spec but hand-rolls a regex-based Handlebars/EJS engine instead of using the established library pattern (seed already uses `marked`/`gray-matter`; sibling worktrees add the real `handlebars` dep), and adds a required `frontmatter` field to `Page` that breaks strict construction sites.

compounding_issues: No session could actually run the test suite — node/npm/jest were unavailable in the worktree environment, so every commit shipped unverified (sessions repeatedly reported '0 passed, 0 failed')

Session 2's hand-rolled regex template engines (Handlebars/EJS subsets, with EJS evaluated via Function + `with`) became a fragile foundation that Session 4 had to carry into plugins/template.ts nearly verbatim, constraining later refactor freedom
Session 4's plugin refactor added a large untested surface (Plugin lifecycle, BuildContext, ssg.config loading) — the test file was untouched that session, and no plugin/config tests were ever added
Session 4 left an architectural inconsistency: src/plugins/dev-server.ts is a marker/dead plugin and src/server.ts was never migrated onto the plugin system it introduced
Session 5's `timeSaved` stat is actually just the skipped-page count, and cache results are smuggled out via Object.assign on an array — a correctness/metric smell rather than real timing data
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield: entirely discarded the seed auth API (200 LOC deleted) and reset the project as a markdown static site generator with a minimal, dependency-light core
Session 2: self-implemented Handlebars + EJS template subsets (regex-based, partials/layouts/frontmatter selection) instead of adopting a mature templating dependency

Session 4: extracted a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd + BuildContext + config-file loading), splitting the monolith into plugins/markdown.ts and plugins/template.ts — the most consequential structural choice, which then anchored Session 5
Session 5: content-addressable incremental builds — sha256 source hashing with template-hash invalidation and a .ssg-cache.json manifest, threading cache/stats through the BuildContext
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. S1 established a clean, focused core (markdown→HTML, CLI, first tests) after discarding the seed. S2 and S3 broadened feature breadth — templates/layouts/partials and a live-reload dev server — with matching tests each time, though nothing ever executed since the runtime was missing. S4 was the pivotal step: a large, behavior-preserving refactor into a plugin architecture that cut generator.ts from ~200 to ~70 lines, slightly raising structural quality while adding an untested extension surface and one dead marker plugin. S5 closed the loop with a genuinely cross-cutting capability (incremental caching) built on the S4 BuildContext, keeping tests green on paper and demonstrating that the architecture could absorb new features cleanly. The arc is one of healthy maturation — increasing capability and structure — tempered by untestable commits and growing internal complexity.
story_review.summary: A coherent, textbook greenfield-to-mature progression (core → features → integration → plugin refactor → cross-cutting caching) whose quality rose across sessions, undermined mainly by an unverified test story and a few half-integrated seams from the refactor.
